title: The Enemy Within
note: This is the enmity that opens the way for the outer enemy and stays hidden inside until that enemy wins. It too must be removed.

couplets.plain: Shade and water are bad for you if they do harm. Your own people’s ways are bad too, if they do you harm.
couplets.pm: Shade and water, which you need, may be sweet at first, yet those that later bring disease are bad. So too the ways of your own people, whom you must embrace: pleasant at first, bad if they later do harm. “Your own people” means kinsmen fit to become enemies within. Their harm is to stay hidden, then ruin you once they have help.

links.quote: Your own people’s ways are bad too, if they do you harm
links.reason: Your own people turn as bad as sickening shade and water when they do you harm.
Being your own earns no exemption: relations are judged by what they do to you.

couplets.plain: Don’t fear enemies who are like swords. Fear the company of enemies who are like kin.
couplets.pm: Don’t fear enemies who stand in the open, like a sword that says it will strike. Fear the friendship of enemies who hide and look like kin. You know the first in advance and can guard against them. The second you can neither know nor guard against, so ruin is certain. The bond they made earlier is worse than any enmity they show later.

links.reason: Fears the foe who looks like kin more than any open attacker.

links.quote: Fear the company of enemies who are like kin

couplets.plain: Fear the enemy within and guard yourself. In your moment of weakness it will slice through you like the tool that cuts a potter’s clay.
couplets.pm: Fear those who have become enemies within, and guard yourself. If you don’t, then when you weaken they will surely ruin you, as a potter’s tool cuts a clay pot. Guarding means keeping them from coming close and not agreeing with them. They show no enmity and cut from underneath, so ruin is sure.

couplets.plain: When an enemy within appears, unsound at heart, it brings many harms that turn your own people bad.
couplets.pm: If a ruler has an enemy within who seems sound on the outside and isn’t inside, it brings him many faults that put his people beyond his control. That enemy turns his kin against him from within. When they turn he can’t trust them, and more follows from that.

couplets.plain: When an enemy within appears who is close by kinship, it brings many harms that lead towards death.
couplets.pm: If a ruler has an enemy within who looks like a relation on the outside, it brings him many faults on the road to death. That enemy backs the outer enemy and, unseen, works treachery such as killing, and wears down the ministers and the other parts of the state.

links.quote: an enemy within appears who is close by kinship

couplets.plain: If discord arises among those close to you, it is always hard to escape death.
couplets.pm: If enmity is born among his own people, it is hard for a ruler ever to avoid death. “Always” means even when he is great in wealth, army and the other parts of the state.

links.quote: it is always hard to escape death
links.reason: Discord among those closest makes death hard to escape, at any time.

couplets.plain: Like a casket and its lid, a family with an enemy within may seem to fit together, but it never joins.
couplets.pm: People of a family with an enemy within may come together like a casket and its lid, with no gap showing outside, yet inside they are not united. Their hearts are divided, so when an outer enemy appears they fall apart. Some read it to mean that the enmity won’t join with the family, or the family with the enmity.

links.quote: may seem to fit together, but it never joins
links.reason: A split family keeps the look of one piece, like a casket and its lid, but is never whole.

couplets.plain: Like gold rubbed by a file, a family with an enemy within wears away its strength.
couplets.pm: A family with an enemy within, however it has grown before, is worn down and loses strength, like iron rubbed by a file. The enemy acts as if working with them, then slowly draws them apart, so their strength wears away.
couplets.note: பொன் is usually gold, and he reads it as iron.

links.reason: An enemy inside a family wears its strength away.

links.quote: Like gold rubbed by a file
links.reason: Gold under the file pictures a family worn away stroke by stroke.

couplets.plain: The enemy within may be as small as a split sesame seed, yet ruin lies inside it.
couplets.pm: A ruler’s enemy within, set beside his greatness, may be as small as a split sesame seed, yet inside it lies the ruin that can destroy all his greatness. That ruin, however great, stays hidden in that tiny enemy until its time, then comes out. So it must not be scorned as small.

links.quote: as small as a split sesame seed
links.reason: No enemy within is too small: one the size of a split sesame seed still holds ruin.

couplets.plain: Living with those who are not of one mind with you is like sharing a hut with a snake.
couplets.pm: Living with those whose hearts don’t agree with yours is like staying with a snake in a small hut. In so small a space, so close, the snake is sure to bite, so your death is certain. So get rid of such people without pity.

links.quote: those who are not of one mind with you
links.reason: Close daily life with those not of one mind with you is a standing danger.

links.quote: sharing a hut with a snake
links.reason: The snake in the hut is a danger too near to step away from.

links.quote: Living with those who are not of one mind with you
